messages:
yusuf: Hey folks, day 2 here. Using Fedora 38 on a company laptop, dotfiles from the repo, asdf for python/node. Installed pre-commit and ran `pre-commit install` but git commits still fail in the editor with: `sh: 1: python: not found` even though `which python` -> ~/.asdf/shims/python in my interactive shell. Also git commit signing with GPG fails in the GUI with `gpg: signing failed: No agent responded`. Anything obvious I'm missing?
elaine: Welcome! Two things: 1) GUI git clients (and some editor integrations) spawn non-login shells that might not source your profile where asdf init runs, so PATH seen by the hook can differ. 2) GPG issues often mean GPG_TTY or agent forwarding not set for GUI processes.
yusuf: Ah ok. I only had `asdf init` in ~/.bashrc and my dotfiles put that behind a helper. What are pragmatic fixes so pre-commit hooks find the correct python?
julia: Quick fixes we've used: a) ensure asdf shims are in ~/.profile or ~/.pam_environment so GUI-launched apps inherit it, or b) add a tiny shim-sourcing wrapper at the top of your git hooks. Example wrapper you can add to `.git/hooks/pre-commit` (make executable):
```
#!/bin/sh
# source the minimal asdf path so pre-commit's shebangs resolve
if [ -f "$HOME/.profile" ]; then
  . "$HOME/.profile"
fi
exec "$@"
```
That just ensures the rest of the hook runs with the same PATH you get in a login shell.
yusuf: Nice. Is it safe to modify the git hooks? pre-commit itself installs a generated hook file, right?
julia: Right, pre-commit generates its own hook, so two options: 1) patch the generated hook to source your profile (tedious on every reinstall), or 2) set `core.hooksPath` to a repo directory you control and drop a small wrapper that sources profile and execs the pre-commit hook from `.git/hooks.d/` (we keep a repo-level hooks dir in dotfiles). Another approach is to put asdf init into `~/.profile`/`~/.pam_environment` so GUI apps see it without hook hacks.
yusuf: Got it. And the GPG agent error? I used gpg2 from homebrew and pinentry-gtk. In terminal `git commit -S` works fine. Only GUI fails.
elaine: GUI apps don't get your tty, so gpg can't prompt. Solution: use gpg-agent with pinentry-curses forwarding or use gpg's gpg-connect-agent and set GPG_TTY in your shell. For GUI git clients, we prefer configuring git to use gpg-agent as a gpg program that doesn't require TTY. Example in `~/.gitconfig`:
```
[gpg]
    program = /usr/bin/gpg
```
And ensure `gpg-agent.conf` has `pinentry-program /usr/bin/pinentry-gtk-2` and the agent is running at login. Some folks set `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in ~/.profile and enable the gnome/keyring agent integration.
precommit-bot: pre-commit: detected failing hook 'python-check' in .git/hooks/pre-commit (exit code 127)
yusuf: Thanks — I moved the asdf init into ~/.profile, restarted X (so GUI apps picked it up), reinstalled pre-commit (`pipx install pre-commit` under asdf python), and now commits from the editor find python. For GPG I changed git to the system gpg and set pinentry program; GUI commit signing now works too.
infra-bot: Created ticket IT-5123: "New-hire: doc update - pre-commit + GUI git clients need asdf init in ~/.profile and GPG agent tips" assigned to julia.
yusuf: Huge help, really appreciate the quick pointers :thumbsup: I'll add a small note to my onboarding PR that you need to restart your session after moving asdf init so GUI apps inherit PATH.
